name: Referral statistics associated with the Building Choices (BC) programme
description: Filter referrals by various associated parameters, So that you can analyse the current state of programme referrals

dataset.name: Referral summary
dataset.query: SELECT c.name AS name, c.audience AS audience, r.status AS status, o.organisation_id, COUNT(r.referral_id) AS referral_count FROM referral r LEFT JOIN offering o ON r.offering_id = o.offering_id LEFT JOIN course c ON o.course_id = c.course_id WHERE r.deleted = FALSE AND (submitted_on) >= (SELECT START_DATE from prompt_) and (submitted_on) <= (SELECT END_DATE from prompt_) GROUP BY CUBE (c.name, c.audience, r.status,o.organisation_id ) ORDER BY c.name

dataset.name: courses
dataset.query: SELECT name FROM public.course WHERE withdrawn = false

dataset.name: prisons
dataset.query: SELECT prison_id as code,name FROM establishment.prison WHERE active = TRUE ORDER by name

dataset.name: individuals
dataset.query: SELECT r.prison_number, forename, surname, gender, location, earliest_release_date, earliest_release_date_type, CASE WHEN earliest_release_date - current_date > 180 THEN 'No' WHEN earliest_release_date - current_date > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'N/A' END AS earliest_release_date_indicator, sentence_type, r.status, referral_id, r.submitted_on, r.additional_information, c.name, c.course_id, rs.closed FROM public.referral r LEFT JOIN person p ON p.prison_number = r.prison_number LEFT JOIN offering o ON o.offering_id = r.offering_id LEFT JOIN course c ON c.course_id = o.course_id LEFT JOIN referral_status rs ON rs.code = r.status

report.name: Table of all referrals
report.description: A table for all referrals, with the ability to subsequently sort and filter the data by any of the fields.
